description: Before the end of your next turn, cast dominate beast or dominate person (rare) or dominate monster (very rare) at DC 15; on a failed save it lasts 1 hour without concentration and the target saves against it with disadvantage.

name: Robe of Summer
description: Resistance to cold, and you're comfortable and unaffected by extreme temperatures.

name: Shatterspike
description: +1 to attack and damage. Hits against objects are automatically critical and can deal bludgeoning or slashing; nonmagical damage can't harm it.

name: Spear of Backbiting
description: +2 to attack and damage; thrown ranges +30 ft., one extra damage die, and it returns to your hand. Curse: you won't part with it and have disadvantage with other weapons; on a natural 1 it strikes you (new attack with advantage against your own AC).

name: Stone of Ill Luck
description: Identifies as a stone of good luck. Curse: -2 to ability checks and saves while carried (applied secretly), and you won't part with it until remove curse.

name: Wand of Entangle
description: 7 charges (regains 1d6 + 1 at dawn; 1 in 20 to crumble when emptied). As an action, spend 1 to cast entangle (DC 13).

name: Wand of the War Mage
description: Adds its bonus to your spell attack rolls, and your spell attacks ignore half cover.

name: Waythe
description: Sentient +1 greatsword (NG; Int 12, Wis 2, Cha 14; hearing and darkvision 120 ft.; speaks Giant and Common, telepathic). Giants it hits take +2d6 slashing and make a DC 15 Str save or fall prone. It also works as a wand of enemy detection that recharges fully at dawn and never crumbles. Good characters attune in 1 minute; it urges bold action.

name: Abracadabrus
description: A gem-studded chest with a 1.5-ft. cubic compartment and 20 charges (regains 1d20 at dawn; 1 in 20 to lose its magic when emptied). As an action, touch the closed lid and spend 1 to conjure named nonmagical objects worth up to 1 gp total that fit inside an empty chest. Food spoils after 24 hours; gems and precious metals vanish after 1 minute.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Cauldron of Plenty
description: A 30-gallon copper cauldron. Stirring water in it for 1 minute turns it into hot stew, one meal for up to four people per gallon; three uses per dawn.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Hook of Fisher's Delight
description: Tied to a line in at least a 10-ft. cube of water, each uninterrupted hour roll a d6; on a 6 a random magical fish appears on the hook. Once per dawn.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Lantern of Tracking
description: A hooded lantern (6 hours per pint of oil, bright light 30 ft., dim 30 ft. more) attuned to one random creature type; its flame turns green while such a creature is within 300 ft.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Orc Stone
description: As an action, summon an orc war chief spirit within 30 ft. that obeys you and understands your languages for 10 minutes or until it drops to 0 HP. After three uses it turns to dust.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Piwafwi (Cloak of Elvenkind)
description: A drow spider-silk cloak of elvenkind: hood up, Perception to see you has disadvantage and you have advantage on Stealth to hide (an action to raise or lower). An hour of unbroken sunlight ruins its magic.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Professor Orb
description: A sentient quartz sphere (Int 18, random Wis and Cha and alignment) that speaks four languages, sees and hears 60 ft., and knows four narrow academic subjects (+9 to recall lore in them). It casts mage hand at will only to move itself and never conflicts with its owner.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Professor Skant
description: A lawful good, chatty, condescending professor orb (Wis 11, Cha 9) speaking Common, Draconic, Elvish, and Loross, expert in Netheril's history, vampires, Elverquisst rituals, and the tarrasque.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Psi Crystal
attunement_note: by a creature with Intelligence 3 or higher
description: Grants telepathy while attuned and glows purple; higher Intelligence means brighter light and longer telepathy range.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Scroll of Tarrasque Summoning
description: As an action, read it to summon the tarrasque within 1 mile, hostile to everything, vanishing at 0 HP.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Scroll of the Comet
description: Outdoors, as an action, call a comet to a point within 1 mile: a 50-ft.-deep, 500-ft.-radius crater; creatures in it make a DC 20 Dex save, 30d10 force or half, and unattended nonmagical objects and structures are destroyed.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Shield Guardian Amulet
description: Linked to one shield guardian, which protects and obeys the wearer; you know its distance and direction on the same plane. Within 10 ft., an action and a DC 20 Arcana check reactivates it. Unattended amulet: AC 10, 10 HP, immune to poison and psychic; a new one costs 1,000 gp and a week.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: The Codicil of White
description: Auril's fur-bound primer of rites: carrying it grants resistance to cold. It holds the spell frost fingers and the incantation poem Rime of the Frostmaiden, which can split a glacier.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Thermal Cube
description: A 3-inch brimstone cube that keeps everything within 15 ft. at 95 degrees Fahrenheit.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Ythryn Mythallar
description: A 50-ft. Netherese crystal globe (bright light 300 ft., dim 300 ft. more); up to eight attune by a short rest within 30 ft., and all must agree to each use. Fly it 30 ft. per action carrying everything within 500 ft.; recharge a held magic item within 30 ft.; cast control weather (50-mile radius) without components. Touching the globe: DC 22 Con save, 180 (20d10 + 70) radiant or half (undead at disadvantage); objects that touch it disintegrate.
book: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden

name: Dawnbringer
description: Sentient gilded hilt (NG; Int 12, Wis 15, Cha 14; hearing and darkvision 120 ft.; speaks Common plus your languages, telepathic). Works as a sun blade, its radiant blade summoned or dismissed as a bonus action. Once per dawn, touch a creature to cast lesser restoration. It fears darkness and abandonment and wants to stay lit and close to you.

name: Piwafwi of Fire Resistance
description: A drow cloak of elvenkind that also grants resistance to fire: hood up (an action), Perception to see you has disadvantage and you have advantage on Stealth to hide. An hour of unbroken sunlight ruins its magic.

name: Spell Gem
attunement_note: by a spellcaster, only to imbue it
description: Holds one spell; if you know it or it's on your class list, cast it from the gem as an action without components (no attunement needed), emptying it. Spells above your level need a spellcasting check (DC 10 + spell level). The gem type sets its maximum spell level, rarity, save DC, and attack bonus. Attuned, cast a 1-action or 1-minute-plus spell into an empty gem to store it (consumed abjuration components at half cost), once per dawn.

name: Stonespeaker Crystal
description: Advantage on Investigation checks. 10 charges (regains 1d6 + 4 at dawn; 1 in 20 to vanish when emptied): speak with animals (2), speak with dead (4), or speak with plants (3). It can replace a consumed material component of a divination spell for 1 charge per spell level.

name: Wand of Viscid Globs
description: 7 charges (regains 1d6 + 1 at midnight; 1 in 20 to melt when emptied). As an action, spend 1 for a ranged attack (spellcasting or Int modifier + proficiency) within 60 ft.; on a hit the target is restrained for 1 hour, ended by a pint of alcohol, oil of etherealness, universal solvent, or sunlight. An hour of unbroken sunlight destroys the wand.

name: Black Crystal Tablet
attunement_note: by a creature proficient in Arcana
description: After attuning, you make a DC 20 Wis save at the end of your next long rest or gain a random long-term madness. As an action, cast eyebite or gate (its portal reaching only the Far Realm) from the tablet; it then can't be used again until the next dawn.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Blast Scepter
description: Works as an arcane focus. While attuned you have resistance to fire and lightning, and as an action you can cast thunderwave at 4th level (DC 16) from it without a slot.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Chest of Preserving
description: A 25-lb. chest, 2.5 ft. by 1.5 ft. by 1 ft. with a rounded lid. Food and other perishables stored inside don't age or spoil.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Circlet of Human Perfection
description: While worn, you look like an attractive human of average build whose features (age, gender, coloring, voice) the circlet picks. Your statistics, racial traits, and gear are unchanged except for size. Taking it off ends the effect.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Dagger of Blindsight
description: A saw-toothed dagger with a black pearl in its pommel. While attuned, you have blindsight 30 ft.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Dodecahedron of Doom
description: A 12-inch, twelve-sided clockwork metal die. As an action, hurl it up to 60 ft.; if it rolls at least 10 ft. before stopping, roll a d12 on its table for a random magical effect (the table is in the adventure). Effects that need a target do nothing without one in range, and spells it casts need no components.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Horn of the Endless Maze
description: As an action, blow it to summon 3d4 + 3 minotaur-like Abyssal spirits within 60 ft. that use berserker stats and leave after 1 hour or at 0 HP. If you are proficient with all simple weapons they obey you and are friendly to your allies; otherwise they attack you. Usable once every 7 days.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Horned Ring
description: Lets the attuned wearer ignore Undermountain's magical restrictions.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Orb of Gonging
description: A hollow 5-inch, 5-lb. orb of notched bronze rings. Spend an action lining up the notches and it gongs loudly every 6 seconds, audible 600 ft. away, until they are knocked out of line.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Potion of Watchful Rest
description: A sweet amber brew. For 8 hours magic can't put you to sleep, and you can stay awake through a long rest and still gain its benefits. It does nothing for creatures that don't sleep.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Propeller Helm
description: While worn, use an action to cast levitate with no components; the propeller whirs loudly until the spell ends. Each time the spell ends, there is a 50 percent chance the helm turns nonmagical.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Shield of the Uven Rune
description: An ancient white dragon scale bearing the uven (enemy) rune, recognizable with a DC 20 Intelligence (History) check. While holding it you are immune to cold; right after a melee hit on you, use your reaction to deal 3d6 necrotic to the attacker; and once per short or long rest you can cast bane (DC 17) from it, lasting 1 minute without concentration. Tracing the rune onto a nonmagical weapon over 8 hours (both within 5 ft.) destroys the shield and makes the weapon a rare +1 weapon requiring attunement, rising to +3 against one creature type you choose: aberrations, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, or undead.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Tearulai
description: A sentient neutral good sword of sharpness with an emerald blade and jeweled hilt, its powers dormant until it is pulled from Valdemar's skull. Hits on objects deal maximum weapon dice. On a natural 20 against a creature it deals 14 extra slashing; roll another d20, and on a 20 it severs a limb (or a chunk of a limbless body). A command word sheds bright light 10 ft. and dim light 10 ft. beyond until repeated or sheathed. An evil creature trying to attune takes 20 psychic. The blade can't be damaged or dulled, and it can't be teleported without its attuned wielder. It has 6 charges (regaining 1d4 + 2 at dawn) to cast fly (2), polymorph (3), or transport via plants (4) without material components. Int 17, Wis 12, Cha 20; hearing and truesight 120 ft.; telepathic with its wielder; speaks Common, Draconic, Elvish, and Sylvan; knows any gem's true value within 5 ft. Vain and beauty-loving, it craves finer gems and longs to return to the forests of Myth Drannor, trying to take over a wielder whose goals oppose that.
book: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage

name: Charm of Plant Command
description: A fist-sized bundle of dried stems bound in silver thread, worn on a thong. It has 3 charges, regaining all at dawn. As an action, spend 1 to cast speak with plants, also gaining advantage on Charisma checks to influence plants for the duration.

name: Cursed Luckstone
description: A cool gray-and-black river stone etched with an unknown sigil. Once per dawn while carrying it, gain advantage on one ability check. Curse: attuning curses you until remove curse or similar magic; you can't get rid of the stone (it teleports back to your pack), and after each use your next two ability checks have disadvantage.

name: Helm of Underwater Action
description: While wearing this brass helmet you can breathe underwater and gain darkvision 60 ft. and a swim speed of 30 ft.

name: Pipe of Remembrance
description: A long wooden pipe with a river-stone bowl. Once per dawn, its smoke lingers around you and after 10 minutes forms moving figures that replay your greatest deeds for 5 minutes before fading.

name: Pressure Capsule
description: A small capsule of beeswax, sand, and enchanted water plants. A creature that eats one ignores the effects of swimming deeper than 100 ft.

name: Sekolahian Worshiping Statuette
description: A 1-ft. sandstone shark with gaping jaws. When a Tiny sea creature comes within 1 inch of its mouth, the shark snaps to life and deals it 1 piercing, at most once per hour.

name: Amulet of the Black Skull
description: An obsidian screaming skull with ruby eyes and emerald teeth on an iron chain. It has 6 charges, regaining 1d6 at dawn. As an action, spend 1 to teleport with your gear to a familiar spot within 100 ft. on the same plane, sight not required; it ignores the Tomb of the Nine Gods' magic restrictions. A non-undead user makes a DC 16 Con save each time or arrives transformed, rolling percentile dice on the Black Skull Transformation table (in the adventure).

name: Bookmark
description: Artus Cimber's +3 dagger. With it drawn, use a bonus action to make its blue pommel gem shed bright light 20 ft. and dim light 20 ft. beyond (or go dark), or turn it into a north-pointing compass on your palm. Once per dawn each, cast dimension door from it, or compulsion (DC 15, range 90 ft., affecting only spiders that are beasts).

name: Ghost Lantern
description: A restless spirit is bound inside. Holding it, command the spirit as a bonus action to shed bright light 30 ft. and dim light 30 ft. beyond, or as an action send it out to act as mage hand until the spell ends. If you fall unconscious within 10 ft., it emerges, stabilizes you, and returns. The spirit can't be harmed, turned, or raised; dispel evil and good frees it to the afterlife and leaves the lantern nonmagical.

name: Mask of the Beast
description: A carved wooden beast mask with 3 charges, regaining all at dawn. While wearing it, spend 1 charge to cast animal friendship as an action.

name: Ring of Winter
description: A frost-rimed gold band that sizes itself and numbs the hand until you attune. Sentient chaotic evil (Int 14, Wis 14, Cha 17; hearing and sight 60 ft.; communicates by emotion), it craves destruction and tries to dominate its wearer into reckless cruelty. Neither ring nor wearer can be targeted by divination or seen through scrying. You don't age while wearing it (age doesn't catch up later), though magical aging still affects you. Attuned, you are immune to cold and extreme cold. 12 charges, regaining all at dawn: 1 as an action to chill a 120-ft.-radius sphere within 300 ft. by 20 degrees per minute down to -30 F, icing surfaces, until you end it as an action; spells (DC 17): sleet storm (1), ice spike growth (1), Bigby's hand of ice dealing bludgeoning as a fist and immune to cold (2), cone of cold (2), ice storm (2), wall of ice (2), flesh to ice as flesh to stone (3), Otiluke's freezing sphere (3); or as an action create within 60 ft. a motionless ice object fitting a 10-ft. cube, hard as metal or stone (2), or an ice copy of a beast of CR 2 or lower (4) that is a construct vulnerable to fire, immune to cold and poison and to charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned, and obeys only you; either melts after 24 hours or at 0 HP, losing 5 (1d10) HP per minute in extreme heat. Rumors claim deeper powers for an evil master it can't break, such as freezing worlds or commanding white dragons and the ice primordial Cryonax. It resists all heat and is destroyed only on the finger of the Summer Queen.

name: Scorpion Armor
description: Plate made from giant scorpion chitin. While worn, you gain +5 to initiative unless incapacitated, and it imposes no disadvantage on Stealth or on saves against extreme heat. Curse: each time you don or doff it, make a DC 15 Con save, taking 100 (10d10 + 45) poison on a failure or half on a success. Only wish lifts the curse.

name: Staff of the Forgotten One
attunement_note: by a sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
description: A crooked bone staff topped by the skull of an archmage Acererak destroyed, marked with his death rune. While you carry it: double proficiency on Arcana and History checks; you can't be blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, petrified, or stunned; undead of CR 2 or lower won't threaten or attack you unless harmed; and it works as a +3 quarterstaff dealing an extra 10 (3d6) necrotic. 7 charges, regaining 1d4 + 3 at dawn: as an action spend 1 to curse a creature within 60 ft. you can see (Con save against your spell DC), which can't regain HP and is vulnerable to necrotic until greater restoration, remove curse, or similar. Whenever anyone but Acererak spends charges, 50 percent chance the trapped archmage tries to possess the wielder (DC 20 Cha save or become a DM-controlled NPC that seeks to destroy the staff; dispel evil and good traps it again). Breaking it as an action unleashes a 30-ft.-radius blast: DC 18 Dex save, 132 (24d10) force, half on success, freeing the spirit. Thrown into a sphere of annihilation, staff, spirit, and sphere are all destroyed without exploding.

name: Yklwa, +1
description: +1 to attack and damage rolls with this magic yklwa, the Chultan short spear: a simple melee weapon dealing 1d8 piercing, thrown at range 10/30 ft.

name: Yklwa, +2
description: +2 to attack and damage rolls with this magic yklwa, the Chultan short spear: a simple melee weapon dealing 1d8 piercing, thrown at range 10/30 ft.

name: Yklwa, +3
description: +3 to attack and damage rolls with this magic yklwa, the Chultan short spear: a simple melee weapon dealing 1d8 piercing, thrown at range 10/30 ft.

name: Blood Spear
description: The chieftain Kavan's blood-stained spear. When your melee attack with it drops a target to 0 HP, you gain 2d6 temporary HP. Anyone can wield it, but only the one Kavan chose gets +2 to attack and damage rolls with it.

name: Crusader's Shortsword
attunement_note: by a lawful good creature (takes 1 minute)
description: A sentient lawful good +1 shortsword (Int 11, Wis 13, Cha 13; hearing and sight 120 ft.; communicates by emotion) devoted to fighting evil. It always sheds bright light 15 ft. and dim light 15 ft. beyond, which only destroying it puts out. Once per dawn, its attuned wielder can cast crusader's mantle from it.

name: Daern's Instant Fortress
description: As an action, set down this 1-inch metal cube and speak its command word; it grows into a 20-ft.-square, 30-ft.-tall adamantine tower with arrow slits, a battlement, two floors joined by a ladder, and a roof trapdoor. Its door faces you, opens only at your command (a bonus action), and resists knock and similar magic. Creatures in the area make a DC 15 Dex save, taking 10d10 bludgeoning or half on success, and are pushed outside; unattended objects take the damage and are pushed. It can't be tipped over. The roof, door, and each wall have 100 HP, immunity to nonmagical non-siege weapons, and resistance to other damage; only wish repairs it, 50 HP to one part per casting. An action and the command word shrink it again, but only while it's empty.

name: Gulthias Staff
description: A spongy black staff cut from a Gulthias tree; beasts within 30 ft. grow uneasy. 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 at dusk. It works as a magic quarterstaff, and on a hit you can spend 1 charge to heal HP equal to its damage, as blood oozes from it and you make a DC 12 Wis save or gain a short-term madness. While attuned, blights and other evil plants don't treat you as hostile unless you harm them. Breaking or burning it unleashes a scream heard 300 ft. away that kills every blight that hears it.

name: Holy Symbol of Ravenkind
attunement_note: by a good-aligned cleric or paladin
description: A sunburst platinum amulet set with a large crystal, once carried by the vampire-hunting paladin Lugdana. 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 at dawn. Hold Vampires (1 charge, action): vampires and vampire spawn within 30 ft. make a DC 15 Wis save or are paralyzed 1 minute, repeating the save each turn end. Turn Undead (3 charges): when presenting it with Turn Undead or Turn the Unholy, undead have disadvantage on their saves. Sunlight (5 charges, action): it sheds sunlight as bright light 30 ft. and dim light 30 ft. beyond for 10 minutes or until you end it.

name: Icon of Ravenloft
description: A 10-lb., 12-inch silver statuette of a kneeling cleric, given to Strahd to consecrate his castle. Every creature within 30 ft. is under protection from evil and good against fiends and undead. Attuned, you can cast augury from it once per dawn without material components; use it as a holy symbol for Turn Undead or Turn the Unholy, raising the save DC by 2; and once per dawn, as an action while holding it, heal a creature you can see within 30 ft. for 3d8 + 3 HP (not undead, constructs, or fiends).

name: Saint Markovia's Thighbone
description: The relic of a saint who wounded Strahd; it works as a mace of disruption. If it hits a vampire or vampire spawn during a battle, it crumbles to dust when that battle ends.

name: Shield of the Silver Dragon
description: A +2 shield bearing the silver dragon emblem of the Order of the Silver Dragon. It whispers warnings, giving you +2 to initiative while you aren't incapacitated.

name: Sunsword
description: The sentient platinum hilt of Sergei von Zarovich's crystal sword, its blade lost forever; it now works as a sun blade. Chaotic good (Int 11, Wis 17, Cha 16; hearing and sight 60 ft.; communicates by emotion). Its purpose is to destroy Strahd, out of revenge for its lost blade, and it secretly fears its own destruction.

name: Yester Hill Axe
description: A battleaxe carved with leaves and vines that weighs half as much as normal. It deals an extra 1d8 slashing to plants and plant creatures. In the hands of a non-good creature it sprouts thorns on each attack, dealing 1 magical piercing to the wielder afterward.

name: Balloon Pack
description: A backpack holding a bound air elemental spirit and a folded leather balloon. While worn, deploy it as an action to levitate yourself for 10 minutes without concentration, or as a reaction when falling to gain feather fall. When the spell ends, the spirit escapes and you sink gently up to 60 ft., falling if still aloft. It works again only after an hour recharging in an elemental air node.

name: Bottled Breath
description: A breath of elemental air. Inhale it and either exhale it for the effect of gust of wind, or hold it and need no air for 1 hour (ending early, as to speak, forfeits the gust).

name: Claws of the Umber Hulk
description: Heavy brown iron gauntlets shaped like umber hulk claws, reaching to the elbows. Wearing both, you gain a 20-ft. burrow speed and tunnel through solid rock at 1 ft. per round. Each claw is a proficient melee weapon dealing 1d8 slashing plus Strength. While wearing them, you can't handle objects or cast spells with somatic components.

name: Devastation Orb
description: A 12-inch, 10-lb. elemental bomb made in a 1-hour ritual at an elemental node with an elemental weapon and 2,000 gp of components; the node sets its element. It detonates 1d100 hours after creation with no outward sign (identify or divination reveals when); it has AC 10, 15 HP, immunity to poison and psychic, and explodes at 0 HP. A case inscribed with the opposing element holds it safely, though removed past its time it blows 1d6 rounds later. Its effect fills a 1-mile-radius sphere, then it is spent. Air: a 1-hour windstorm; creatures ending a turn exposed make a DC 18 Con save or take 1d4 bludgeoning, light structures and weak trees fall after 10 minutes, and strong wind rules apply. Earth: earthquake (DC 18) for 1 minute. Fire: a 24-hour extreme-heat wave with a 10 percent chance each hour of a spreading wildfire that deals 3d6 fire to creatures coming within 10 ft. Water: 24 hours of heavy rain; a substantial body of water floods after 2d10 hours, rising 10 ft. and surging outward 100 ft. per round, sweeping away Large or smaller creatures and light structures.

name: Drown
description: A barnacle-studded steel trident holding a spark of Olhydra; it floats, stays cool, and water never harms it. +1 to attack and damage, and hits deal an extra 1d8 cold. While you hold it, you speak Aquan, resist cold, and once per dawn can cast dominate monster (DC 17) on a water elemental. Once per dawn inside a water node, you can perform the Tears of Endless Anguish ritual to make a water devastation orb. Flaw while attuned: you demand the largest share of spoils and part with nothing; after 24 hours attuned, barnacles grow on your skin until greater restoration (not while attuned).

name: Ironfang
description: A rune-etched iron war pick holding a spark of Ogrémoch, immune to rust, acid, and corrosion. +2 to attack and damage, and hits deal an extra 1d8 thunder. While you hold it, you speak Terran, resist acid, have tremorsense 60 ft., sense (but can't pinpoint) precious metals and stones within 60 ft., and once per dawn can cast dominate monster (DC 17) on an earth elemental. 3 charges, regaining 1d3 at dawn: spend 1 as an action to cast 2nd-level shatter (DC 17). Once per dawn inside an earth node, you can perform the Rumbling ritual to make an earth devastation orb. Flaw while attuned: you love to break things and cause ruin.

name: Lost Crown of Besilmer
description: An open-faced steel dwarven helm ringed by a gold circlet with seven spikes. While worn, you resist psychic damage and have advantage on saves against being charmed. 3 charges, regaining 1d3 at dawn: as a bonus action, spend 1 to inspire a creature within 60 ft. that can see or hear you, which can add a d6 to one ability check, attack roll, or save before the end of your next turn.

name: Orcsplitter
attunement_note: by a good-aligned dwarf, fighter, or paladin
description: King Torhild Flametongue's battered greataxe, its rune for orc split in two. While you hold it: +2 to attack and damage; a natural 20 against an orc forces a DC 17 Con save or it drops to 0 HP; orcs can't surprise you while you aren't incapacitated, and you sense orcs within 120 ft. not behind total cover (not where); and you and friends within 30 ft. can't be frightened while you aren't incapacitated. Sentient lawful good (Int 6, Wis 15, Cha 10; sight and hearing 120 ft. with darkvision), it speaks through emotion and the odd verse of old Dwarvish. Grim and unbending, it scorns cowardice and deceit, exists to defend dwarves, and urges you against giants, goblins, and above all orcs.

name: Seeker Dart
description: A dart etched with wind spirals. Whisper 'seek' and throw it at a creature within 120 ft. that you've seen before (sight not needed now); with a clear path, winds carry it instantly through 1-inch gaps and around corners. The target makes a DC 16 Dex save or takes 1d4 piercing and 3d4 lightning. Then, or if there's no path, it becomes an ordinary dart.

name: Storm Boomerang
description: A griffon-bone boomerang marked with the air sigil; a thrown ranged weapon (60/120 ft.) usable by anyone proficient with javelins. A hit deals 1d4 bludgeoning and 3d4 thunder, and the target makes a DC 10 Con save or is stunned until the end of its next turn; a miss returns it to your hand. After dealing thunder once, it loses the thunder and stun until it spends an hour in an elemental air node.

name: Tinderstrike
description: A keen flint dagger holding a spark of Imix; it throws sparks on solid hits, stays warm, and smolders 1d4 minutes after drawing blood. +2 to attack and damage, and hits deal an extra 2d6 fire. While you hold it, you speak Ignan, resist fire, and once per dawn can cast dominate monster (DC 17) on a fire elemental. Once per dawn inside a fire node, you can perform the Dance of the All-Consuming Fire ritual to make a fire devastation orb. Flaw while attuned: you act without thinking and take reckless risks.

name: Weird Tank
description: A ten-gallon glass-and-bronze tank on a leather harness, holding a water weird. While wearing it, open it as an action to release the weird, which acts right after you, stays bound to the tank, and obeys your telepathic commands (no action). You can close it as an action only after the weird retracts or dies. If the weird dies, the tank works again only after 24 hours in an elemental water node, which forms a new weird. The tank has AC 15, 50 HP, vulnerability to bludgeoning, and immunity to poison and psychic; destroying it kills the weird.

name: Windvane
description: A silver spear set with dark sapphires, light as a breeze, holding a spark of Yan-C-Bin. +2 to attack and damage, it has the finesse property, and hits deal an extra 1d6 lightning. While you hold it, you speak Auran, resist lightning, and once per dawn can cast dominate monster (DC 17) on an air elemental. Once per dawn inside an air node, you can perform the Song of the Four Winds ritual to make an air devastation orb. Flaw while attuned: you break vows and plans, caring nothing for duty or honor.

name: Wingwear
description: A snug, air-embroidered suit with gliding flaps. 3 charges: as a bonus action, spend 1 to gain a 30-ft. fly speed until you land. You lose 5 ft. of altitude at the end of each turn, or drop to the ground at once if you didn't fly 30 ft. horizontally that turn; landing ends it. It recharges fully after an hour in an elemental air node.

name: Bobbing Lily Pad
description: A 10-ft.-wide floating leaf vehicle whose tendrils carry it over land, across water (not under it), and through the air at walk, fly, and swim speeds of 20 ft., with hover, following your spoken directions while you ride. It carries 300 lb. freely, or up to double that at half speed.

name: Chromatic Rose
description: A magic rose in one of five colors, each tied to a damage type (acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison) and showing a harmless visual effect when held. Held by the stem, it gives you resistance to its type; if a single source would still deal you more than 10 of that type, the rose disintegrates and you take none. As an action, blow its petals into a 20-ft. cone of its element: DC 15 Con save, 3d10 of that type, half on success, destroying the rose.

name: Dust of Corrosion
description: One packet of ground rust monster antennae. As an action, throw it to fill a 10-ft. cube from you: nonmagical ferrous metal there rusts instantly to useless dust, and creatures made wholly or partly of ferrous metal make a DC 13 Con save, 4d8 necrotic, half on success.

name: Eldritch Staff
description: A +1 quarterstaff with 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 at dawn; spending the last, roll a d20, and on a 1 it bursts harmlessly and is destroyed. On a melee hit you can spend up to 3 charges for an extra 1d8 lightning each. When you take damage while holding it, use your reaction and 3 charges to turn invisible and teleport with your gear up to 60 ft. to a space you can see, staying invisible until your next turn starts or you attack, cast a spell, or deal damage.

name: Iggwilv's Cauldron
description: An 80-lb., 100-gallon cauldron on eight clawed feet that only Iggwilv or Baba Yaga can switch (with an action and a touch) between a gold form, embossed with bare trees, leaves, and brooms, and an iron form, embossed with eight each of bats, toads, cats, lizards, and snakes. A humanoid attuning makes a DC 15 Con save or is aged to frailty (half speed, sight and hearing limited to 30 ft., disadvantage on checks, attacks, and saves, and death of old age in 3d8 days), reversible only by wish or divine intervention; a hag coven of three can attune together until it disbands. It has one minor beneficial and one minor detrimental random property. Gold: stirred water becomes hot stew feeding four per gallon; once per dawn, wine stirred 10 minutes becomes an elixir giving four per gallon 10 temporary HP (vanishing after an hour); filled with 90 gallons of water and 10 of wine, it focuses a scrying that the target automatically fails, even across planes, consuming the liquid; once per dawn, a broom dipped in it becomes a broom of flying for 3 days. Iron: once per dawn, scream into it as an action to release an obedient swarm of bats for 1 minute, acting after you; once per dawn, a gallon or more of blood stirred 1 minute puts humanoids within 100 ft. per gallon to sleep for 1 hour (not attuned or charm-immune creatures), waking on damage or a shake; once per 8 days, a branch tipped with a dead frog or toad and dipped in water becomes a wand of polymorph with 3 charges that crumbles when emptied; touching it with a unicorn horn for 1 minute while reciting the poem The Witch Queen's Cauldron freezes every unattuned creature within 1,000 ft. in time (helpless, unaware, untouchable, and unaffected by magic) until the ritual is repeated, the cauldron is destroyed or leaves the plane, or a frozen creature meets an antimagic field or a unicorn horn. It is a Medium object (AC 19, 80 HP) harmed only by a flame tongue or frost brand; at 0 HP it shatters into eight pieces, ending its effects and stripping every hag coven in the multiverse of Shared Spellcasting until a wish reassembles the pieces within 5 ft. of one another.

name: Ornithopter of Flying
description: An 8-ft.-long, 25-lb. flying contraption with a 14-ft. wingspan. It carries a rider of up to 300 lb. (with gear) at a fly speed of 30 ft. by spoken directions, but can't hover. If it loses its rider while aloft, it falls and can't fly again for 1d6 + 4 days.

name: Pixie Dust
description: One packet. As an action, sprinkle it on yourself or a creature you can see within 5 ft. to grant a 30-ft. fly speed with hover for 1 minute; if aloft when it ends, the creature floats safely to the ground.

name: Potion of Advantage
description: A sparkling golden mist that pours like water. After drinking it, you have advantage on one ability check, attack roll, or save of your choice within the next hour.

name: Scissors of Shadow Snipping
attunement_note: by a fey or a spellcaster
description: Iron shears. Once per dawn, as an action, snip away the shadow of a humanoid you can see within 5 ft. (an unwilling target keeps it with a DC 15 Cha save). The shadow stays rooted until you use a bonus action, while you can see it, either to steer it up to 30 ft. across any solid or liquid surface (harmless, unharmable, invisible in darkness, silent, needing nothing) or to release it, after which it acts on its own as a fey shadow whose Strength Drain knocks creatures unconscious at 0 Strength rather than killing them (recovering after a rest). A shadowless creature is cursed until a curse-ending spell or the shadow's destruction returns its shadow.

name: Snicker-Snack
description: A +3 vorpal greatsword that ignores resistance to slashing. On a natural 20 against a creature with a head, it lops one off, killing it if it can't live without it; creatures immune to slashing, headless, with legendary actions, or too big instead take an extra 6d8 slashing. While attuned you're proficient with greatswords and can use Charisma for its attack and damage rolls. Sentient chaotic good (Int 9, Wis 14, Cha 18; hearing and darkvision 120 ft.; speaks, reads, and understands Common in a silvery voice), it craves slaying evil dragons. Fickle, it ends attunement after you miss three times in a row; after each long rest you can win it back with a contested Charisma check, and in no other way.

name: Steel
description: A +2 longsword. Once per dawn, as an action, cast revivify from it by touching the target with the blade. Sentient lawful good (Int 8, Wis 11, Cha 15; sight and hearing 60 ft.; speaks, reads, and understands Common and Draconic), it frets over your welfare and hates backing down from a fight.

name: Witchlight Vane
attunement_note: by Mister Light or his chosen successor
description: A 3-lb. rod set with red glass and topped with butterfly wings. Attuned, it is a +3 mace dealing an extra 1d8 radiant. Within the Witchlight Carnival it senses the mood of every creature of Int 4 or higher; as an action you can pinpoint the happiest, and its wings turn clockwise when spirits are high and counterclockwise when they're low. Sentient chaotic good (Int 11, Wis 14, Cha 14; sight and hearing 30 ft.; communicates by emotion), it wants everyone at the carnival enjoying themselves. Its holder is vulnerable to lightning; its attuned bearer can't be blinded, deafened, petrified, or stunned and can cast dancing lights, polymorph, or ray of frost as an action without components using Charisma (after each polymorph roll a d8; on a 3 or 8, no more polymorph until dawn).

name: Witchlight Watch
attunement_note: by Mister Witch or his chosen successor
description: A glowing gold pocket watch on a chain, ticking only for its holder, whose face shows the carnival ringed by a tiny henge whose moving shadows mark the time. As an action, its attuned owner can start packing up or setting up the whole Witchlight Carnival on the same plane; over 1 hour every carnival object moves itself into place, creatures are unaffected, the process can't be stopped, and the property is then unusable for 8 hours. The attuned bearer can cast fire bolt, invisibility, or message as an action without components using Intelligence (after each invisibility roll a d8; on a 3 or 8, no more invisibility until dawn), gains 30 lb. while attuned, and must eat and drink eight times the normal amount each day.

name: Woodcutter's Axe
description: A +1 greataxe that deals an extra 2d6 slashing on hits against plants, plant creatures, and unattended wooden objects.

name: Cracked Driftglobe
description: A 1-lb. sphere of thick, cracked glass. Within 60 ft. of it, speak its command word to make it shed light as the light spell.

name: Gloves of Soul Catching
description: While worn, your Constitution is 20 (no effect if already 20 or higher). After a successful unarmed strike, you can deal an extra 2d10 force and either regain HP equal to that force damage or gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or save before the end of your next turn.

name: Iron Bands of Bilarro
description: A rusty 3-inch, 1-lb. iron ball. Once per dawn, as an action, speak its command word and hurl it at a Huge or smaller creature you can see within 60 ft., making a ranged attack with Dex plus proficiency. On a hit, it unfolds into bands that restrain the target until you speak the word again as a bonus action; a miss or release returns it to a ball. Any creature can use an action and a DC 20 Strength check to snap the bands, destroying them; a failure bars that creature from trying again for 24 hours.

name: Nether Scroll of Azumar
description: A scroll that isn't used up. After 30 days of study (8 hours a day), make a DC 25 Intelligence (Arcana) check; failure deals 16d10 psychic and requires another 30 days before retrying. On success your Intelligence rises by 2 (max 22, once only), you gain advantage on saves against spells and magical effects, and a stone golem appears within 60 ft. as your ally, crumbling to dust if you die.

name: Orcus Figurine
description: A gray figurine of Orcus carved from an ogre's petrified heart, reeking of rot within 5 ft. It is a Tiny object (AC 17, 3 HP) immune to all damage but radiant, and detect evil and good reveals it as desecrated. While intact: undead within 30 ft. can't be turned, and dead creatures within 30 ft. can't be revived. Praying to Orcus while holding it for at least an hour has a 10 percent chance to summon a smoky avatar (wraith stats, chaotic evil) that attacks every non-undead it meets and vanishes after 1 hour or at 0 HP; once summoned, it can't be called again for 30 days.

name: Radiance
description: A golden hand mirror that serves as a wand. While held, +1 to spell attack rolls, and your spell attacks ignore half cover. It sheds dim light 5 ft. when surrounded by darkness. Once per dawn, as a bonus action, cast enhance ability on yourself only.

name: Serpent Scale Armor
description: Shimmering scale mail. You add your full Dexterity modifier to AC instead of a maximum of +2, and it imposes no disadvantage on Stealth.

name: Serpent's Fang
description: A single-edged magic sword carved from a giant serpent's fang, its hilt reshaping to fit any hand. Hits deal an extra 1d10 poison.

name: Staff of Fate
description: A clear crystal +3 quarterstaff with 6 charges. As a bonus action, spend 1 to give yourself or a creature you can see a d4 to add to one ability check, attack roll, damage roll, or save before your next turn starts (lost if unused). Spending the last charge, roll a d20: on 9 or lower it becomes a plain quarterstaff that shatters on its first damaging hit; on 10 or higher it regains 1d6 charges.

name: Stonky's Ring
description: While worn, cast telekinesis at will, targeting only unattended objects. Its attuned wearer commands Stonky's constructs, though skitterwidgets ignore commands spoken from more than 30 ft. away.

name: Watchful Helm
description: While worn: +1 AC, awareness of your surroundings even while asleep, and advantage on sight-based Perception. Once per dawn, as a bonus action, cast see invisibility from it.

name: Battle Standard of Infernal Power
description: A hell-forged infernal iron banner bearing a small sealed cage with an incapacitated quasit inside (cage AC 19, 10 HP, immune to all but force). If the quasit dies or escapes, it vanishes in smoke and a new one appears while the cage is intact. While you hold it, your weapon attacks and those of allies within 300 ft. count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity.

name: Blade of Avernus
description: Works as a vorpal sword, with 2 minor beneficial, 1 major beneficial, and 1 major detrimental random property (the last suppressed while an archdevil is attuned). Ruler of Avernus: as an action, point it at a devil you can see within 60 ft., which makes a DC 22 Cha save or is charmed for 1 hour and obeys you; ordering it toward what it sees as suicide ends the charm and the sword can't target that devil again. Infernal Recall: as an action, cast word of recall, delivering creatures within 30 ft. of the current ruler of Avernus, or to a sanctuary you choose if you rule it. Destroyed by casting it into the River Styx or melting it in the forge that made it.

name: Fane-Eater
attunement_note: by an evil cleric or paladin
description: Arkhan the Cruel's battleaxe. +3 to attack and damage; on a natural 20 against a creature, it takes an extra 2d8 necrotic and you regain that much HP.

name: Gauntlets of Flaming Fury
description: Steel gauntlets. Wearing both, any nonmagical weapon you hold in them counts as magical. Once per dawn, as a bonus action, wreathe one or two held melee weapons in flame, each dealing an extra 1d6 fire on hits until you sheathe or let go of either.

name: Hellfire Weapon
description: A weapon of infernal iron veined with hellfire that sheds dim light 5 ft. A humanoid killed by it has its soul drawn into the River Styx, where it is instantly reborn as a lemure.

name: Helm of Devil Command
attunement_note: by a creature that speaks Infernal
description: A bulky, eyeless pit fiend helm that resizes to fit; you see through it normally. You know the location and kind of every devil within 1,000 ft. and can speak telepathically to one or broadcast to all (they can't reply). 3 charges, all returning 24 hours after the last is spent: as an action, spend 1 to cast dominate monster (DC 21) on a devil only (a non-devil target wastes the charge), and a devil that sees you knows you tried. A non-devil using this in the Nine Hells has a 20 percent chance of drawing a narzugon on a nightmare within 1d4 hours, intent on reclaiming the helm for its master.

name: Infernal Puzzle Box
description: A 3-lb., 5- to 6-inch airtight cube of infernal iron, bone, or horn used to hold diabolic contracts. An object placed inside is sealed in; no magic can open the box, and it becomes immune to damage. Each opens by its own mundane trick, which a creature that knows it can perform as an action. Studying it for an hour allows a DC 30 Intelligence (Investigation) check to learn the trick; failing by 5 or more forces a DC 18 Wis save, 42 (12d6) psychic, half on success.

name: Infernal Tack
description: A narzugon's full nightmare harness: bridle, bit, reins, saddle, stirrups, and spurs. A nightmare wearing it serves the spur-wearer until that wearer dies or the tack is removed. As an action, clash the spurs or scrape them through blood to call it; it arrives within 20 ft. at the start of your next turn, acts on your initiative as your ally, and stays 1 day, until either of you dies, or until you dismiss it as an action. If it dies, it re-forms in the Nine Hells in 24 hours and can be called again. A nightmare must first be subdued to be harnessed.

name: Matalotok
description: The Frost Father, forged by the frost giant god Thrym and favored by Kostchtchie; icy and wreathed in mist. While you hold it you are immune to cold, and whenever it damages a creature, it releases a 30-ft.-radius burst dealing 10 (3d6) cold to each creature there.

name: Obsidian Flint Dragon Plate
description: Plate armor granting +2 AC, resistance to poison, and advantage on checks and saves to avoid or escape being grappled.

name: Shield of the Hidden Lord
description: A celestial shield, now twisted into a shifting fiendish face, that imprisons the pit fiend Gargauth. While holding it you gain +2 AC and resistance to fire. While Gargauth is inside it is sentient (Int 22, Wis 18, Cha 24; hearing and truesight 120 ft.; speaks Common and Infernal in a hollow whisper; telepathic within 120 ft.). 3 charges, regaining all at dawn: as an action spend 1 for fireball or 2 for wall of fire lasting 1 minute without concentration (DC 21). Once per dawn, on its own choice during your turn, it radiates dread for 1 minute: hostile creatures starting their turn within 20 ft. make a DC 18 Wis save or are frightened until their next turn, immune for 24 hours on success. Calling itself the Hidden Lord, Gargauth hints it is a trapped angel, steers its bearer toward cruelty and domination, and wrongly believes it can escape in the Nine Hells. Dispel evil and good has a 1 percent chance to free it (certain if cast by a solar, planetar, or archdevil), or a god can free it by touch and name.

name: Smokepowder
description: A magical explosive for firearms, kept in waterproof packets (five shots) or airtight kegs (five hundred). Set alight, dropped, or handled roughly, it explodes, dealing fire to everything within 20 ft.: 1d6 for a packet, 9d6 for a keg, halved with a DC 12 Dex save. Dispel magic renders it permanently inert.

name: Soul Coin
description: A 5-inch, third-of-a-pound infernal iron coin inscribed in Infernal that binds one soul, which you can feel raging or despairing. Evil creatures can carry any number; a non-evil creature carrying more than its Constitution modifier has disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saves. 3 charges: as an action, spend 1 to drain 1d10 temporary HP from the soul, or to ask it a question it must answer truthfully in a sentence or two from what it knew in life. A curse-removing spell or spending the last charge frees the soul and rusts the coin away, as does destroying it (AC 19, 1 HP per remaining charge, harmed only by a hellfire weapon or an infernal war machine's furnace). Freed souls go to their god's realm or alignment plane; lawful evil ones usually rise from the Styx as lemures. Freeing a soul is a good act. They are the currency of the Nine Hells, minted by Mammon on Minauros.

name: Sword of Zariel
attunement_note: by a creature the sword deems worthy
description: The fallen Zariel's celestial-steel longsword, glowing faintly and humming; it seeks a brave, heroic wielder and allows attunement immediately. Your first attunement permanently transforms you into an idealized, heavenly self (no magic reverses it): your alignment becomes lawful good, you speak, read, and write Celestial, resist necrotic and radiant, your Charisma becomes 20 (if lower), you grow feathered wings (fly 90 ft., hover), you gain truesight 60 ft., and you take new personality traits rolled on its tables. It sheds bright light 5 ft. and dim light 5 ft. beyond (15 and 15 as a bonus action, or back); fiends have disadvantage on attacks within its bright light. It has 2 minor beneficial random properties and deals an extra 9 (2d8) radiant, or 16 (3d10) two-handed, and an evil creature damaged by it makes a DC 17 Con save or is blinded until the end of its next turn. Sentient lawful good (Int 10, Wis 20, Cha 18; sight and hearing 30 ft.; communicates by emotion); while held, advantage on Insight checks. Zariel can destroy it by grasping it, and it is destroyed if used to shatter the Companion unless wielded by an angel of CR 15+ or a good cleric or paladin of 10th level or higher; if Zariel dies in the Nine Hells, it becomes as breakable as any longsword.

name: Black Dragon Mask
description: A glossy ebony mask with horns and a skull-like look that reshapes to fit its wearer. While worn and attuned: resistance to acid (immunity if you already resist it; if already immune, acid damage instead heals you for half of it); unarmored, add your Charisma bonus to AC; a breath weapon that needs a rest to recharge gains recharge 6; darkvision 60 ft. (or +60 ft. if you have it) and, once per day, blindsight 30 ft. for 5 minutes; you speak and understand Draconic and have advantage on Charisma checks against black dragons; and once per day you can turn a failed save into a success. You can also breathe underwater.

name: Blue Dragon Mask
description: A glossy azure mask ringed with spikes and crowned by a ridged horn that reshapes to fit its wearer. While worn and attuned: resistance to lightning (immunity if you already resist it; if already immune, lightning damage instead heals you for half of it); unarmored, add your Charisma bonus to AC; a breath weapon that needs a rest to recharge gains recharge 6; darkvision 60 ft. (or +60 ft. if you have it) and, once per day, blindsight 30 ft. for 5 minutes; you speak and understand Draconic and have advantage on Charisma checks against blue dragons; and once per day you can turn a failed save into a success. Creatures you deal lightning damage to can't take reactions until their next turn.

name: Green Dragon Mask
description: A mottled green mask with a frilled crest and spiked jaw plates that reshapes to fit its wearer. While worn and attuned: resistance to poison (immunity if you already resist it; if already immune, poison damage instead heals you for half of it); unarmored, add your Charisma bonus to AC; a breath weapon that needs a rest to recharge gains recharge 6; darkvision 60 ft. (or +60 ft. if you have it) and, once per day, blindsight 30 ft. for 5 minutes; you speak and understand Draconic and have advantage on Charisma checks against green dragons; and once per day you can turn a failed save into a success. You can also breathe underwater.

name: Red Dragon Mask
description: A glossy crimson mask with swept-back horns and spiked cheek ridges that reshapes to fit its wearer. While worn and attuned: resistance to fire (immunity if you already resist it; if already immune, fire damage instead heals you for half of it); unarmored, add your Charisma bonus to AC; a breath weapon that needs a rest to recharge gains recharge 6; darkvision 60 ft. (or +60 ft. if you have it) and, once per day, blindsight 30 ft. for 5 minutes; you speak and understand Draconic and have advantage on Charisma checks against red dragons; and once per day you can turn a failed save into a success. Creatures and flammable objects you deal fire damage to catch fire, taking 1d6 fire at the start of each of their turns until someone in reach uses an action to put it out.

name: White Dragon Mask
description: A gleaming white mask touched with pale blue under a spined crest that reshapes to fit its wearer. While worn and attuned: resistance to cold (immunity if you already resist it; if already immune, cold damage instead heals you for half of it); unarmored, add your Charisma bonus to AC; a breath weapon that needs a rest to recharge gains recharge 6; darkvision 60 ft. (or +60 ft. if you have it) and, once per day, blindsight 30 ft. for 5 minutes; you speak and understand Draconic and have advantage on Charisma checks against white dragons; and once per day you can turn a failed save into a success. While at half your HP maximum or lower, your melee attacks deal an extra 1d8 cold.

name: Draakhorn
description: The horn of Ephelomon, Tiamat's ancient red dragon consort, given to dragons for their war on the giants. So huge that two Medium creatures (or one Large or bigger) must hold it while a third sounds it, it makes the ground thrum; its low drone unsettles animals for miles and warns every dragon within 2,000 miles of great danger. Coded blasts once sent specific messages. Made to warn chromatic dragons, it is now misused by the Cult of the Dragon to summon them to the Well of Dragons.

name: Dragongleam
description: A spear holding 10 charges of daylight, meant for dim forest undergrowth, triggered by the Draconic command phrase 'Tiamat's eyes shine' inscribed on its crossguard.

name: Dragontooth Dagger
description: A dagger made from a dragon's fang with a leather-wrapped root for a handle and no crossguard. +1 to attack and damage, and hits deal an extra 1d6 acid; against enemies of the Cult of the Dragon the bonus becomes +2 and the acid 2d6.

name: Hazirawn
description: A sentient neutral evil greatsword that speaks Common and Netherese. Unattuned, it gives +1 to attack and damage and deals an extra 1d6 necrotic on hits. Attuned, the bonus is +2 and the necrotic 2d6, and a creature you hit can't regain HP for 1 minute, ending early on a DC 15 Con save at the end of each of its turns. Attuned and in hand, use an action to spend charges (4, regaining 1d4 at midnight) to cast detect magic (1), detect evil and good (1), or detect thoughts (2).

name: Insignia of Claws
description: A jeweled Cult of the Dragon insignia that flares purple as combat begins. While worn, your unarmed strikes and natural weapons gain +1 to attack and damage rolls and count as magical.

name: Mask of the Dragon Queen
description: Bringing two or more dragon masks together fuses them into this crown of five roaring chromatic heads over a new draconic mask covering face, neck, and shoulders. While worn and attuned: resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning, and poison (each becoming immunity if you already resist it, or healing you for half the damage if already immune); unarmored, add your Charisma bonus to AC; a breath weapon needing a rest gains recharge 6; darkvision 60 ft. (or +60 ft.) and once per day blindsight 30 ft. for 5 minutes; you speak Draconic; and five times per day you can turn a failed save into a success. You also gain the color-specific benefits of one mask of your choice, including advantage on Charisma checks against dragons of that color: Dragon Fire (red), Lingering Shock (blue), Water Breathing (black or green), or Winter's Fury (white).

name: Tankard of Plenty
description: A golden stein decorated with dancing dwarves and grain. 3 charges, regaining all at dawn: grasp the handle and say 'Illefarn' to spend 1 and fill it with three pints of rich dwarven ale.

name: Wand of Winter
description: An icicle-like wand with 7 charges, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dawn; spending the last, roll a d20, and on a 20 it melts away. As an action, cast from it even if you can't cast spells, with no components: ray of frost (free, or 1 charge at 5th level; +5 to hit), sleet storm (3 charges, DC 15), or ice storm (4 charges, DC 15).

name: Bracers of Celerity
description: Lightweight bronze bracers lined with purple velvet. While wearing them, all your speeds increase by 10 feet, and you have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the paralyzed or restrained condition on yourself.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Cape of Enlargement
description: A grayish-purple cape with silver runes along its hem. It has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. As a bonus action, expend 1 charge to enlarge yourself for 10 minutes (or until you dismiss it as a bonus action): your size increases by one category (or as large as the space allows), you have advantage on Strength checks and saving throws, and your weapon and unarmed strike hits add your proficiency bonus to damage.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Dragonguard
description: You have a +1 bonus to AC while wearing this armor. Made for Tergon, a human hero of old Neverwinter, this breastplate bears a gold dragon motif and grants advantage on saving throws against the breath weapons of dragons.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Flayer Slayer
description: Carvings of decapitated mind flayers adorn the blade. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this greataxe. An aberration hit with it takes an extra 1d12 slashing damage, and if it is grappling a creature it must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or release each creature it is grappling.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Hew
description: A +1 battleaxe that deals maximum damage when its wielder attacks a plant creature or an object made of wood. Its creator used it for protection in the forest while cutting firewood.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Lightbringer
description: A +1 mace made for a cleric of Lathander, its solid brass head shaped like a sunburst. On command it glows as bright as a torch, and while glowing it deals an extra 1d6 radiant damage to undead.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Luminous War Pick
description: The haft is inlaid with crushed pearlescent stones that give it a faint glow. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this war pick. As a bonus action you can cast daylight centered on a point on the pick; this can't be used again until the next dawn.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Mind Crystal
description:
A gemstone holding a single-use spell modification. When you cast a spell with a casting time of 1 action while holding it, you can modify the spell as described below; only one mind crystal per spell, and not alongside a Metamagic option. Afterward it becomes a nonmagical gem worth 50 gp.
Careful (Uncommon): up to three creatures affected by the spell automatically succeed on their saves against it.
Distant (Uncommon): a spell with a range of 5 feet or more (not self) gains 100 feet of range; a touch spell gets a range of 30 feet.
Empowered (Uncommon): reroll up to three damage dice, using the new rolls.
Extended (Uncommon): a spell lasting 1 minute or longer has its duration doubled, to a maximum of 24 hours.
Heightened (Rare): one creature affected by the spell has disadvantage on its first save against it.
Quickened (Rare): the casting time becomes 1 bonus action.
Subtle (Common): cast the spell without verbal or somatic components.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Mindblasting Cap
description: A soft violet cap stitched with the folds of a brain. As a bonus action while wearing it, project psychic energy in a 60-foot cone: each creature there makes a DC 15 Intelligence saving throw, taking 5d8 psychic damage and becoming stunned for 1 minute on a failure (repeating the save at the end of each of its turns), or half damage only on a success. Once used, this can't be used again until the next dawn.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Mindguard Crown
description: While you wear this adamantine crown, you have advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws, and resistance to psychic damage.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Mudslick Tower
description:
As an action, place this 1-inch granite sphere on the ground and speak its Terran command word ("petrification") to make it grow into a tower 20 feet on a side and 30 feet high, with arrow slits, a battlement, two floors joined by a ladder, and a roof trapdoor. Speak the word again while touching it to shrink it back; it must be empty. Muddy knobs constantly extrude and retract across its surface.
Each creature in the area where it appears makes a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 10d10 bludgeoning damage on a failure or half on a success, and is pushed to an unoccupied space next to the tower; unworn objects take the damage and are pushed automatically. When it expands it merges with any natural stone it touches.
Its small door faces you and opens only at your command (a bonus action), and is immune to knock and similar magic. The tower is adamantine and can't be tipped over. The roof, door, and each wall have 100 hit points, immunity to damage from nonmagical weapons other than siege weapons, and resistance to all other damage; while merged with natural stone it is immune to all damage. Only a wish spell can repair it, restoring 50 hit points to the roof, door, or one wall per casting.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Netherese Ring of Protection
description: Made from a single piece of mystical green glass stronger than steel. You gain a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws while wearing it, plus a +4 bonus to saving throws or checks to avoid dropping or being disarmed of anything held in that hand.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Potion of Psionic Fortitude
description: When you drink this black potion swirling with pink and purple flecks, you have advantage for 1 hour on saving throws to avoid or end the charmed or stunned condition on yourself.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Ring of the Orator
description: This ring has 6 charges and regains 1d6 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing it, expend 1 charge to project your voice clearly to all creatures within 1 mile for 1 minute, regardless of noise; magical silence, 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood blocks it. Creatures you can see understand you even if they don't know the language you speak.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Spider Staff
attunement_note: by a bard, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
description:
The top of this magic quarterstaff is shaped like a spider, and it deals an extra 1d6 poison damage on a hit when used to make a weapon attack.
Spells. The staff has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dusk. While holding it, you can expend charges to cast spider climb (1 charge) or web (2 charges; save DC 15). If you expend the last charge, roll a d20; on a 1, the staff crumbles to dust.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Staff of Defense
attunement_note: by a bard, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
description:
This slender, hollow 3-pound staff is made of glass yet is as strong as oak. While holding it, you have a +1 bonus to AC.
Spells. The staff has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, you can expend charges to cast mage armor (1 charge) or shield (2 charges). If you expend the last charge, roll a d20; on a 1, the staff shatters.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Statuette of Augury
description: A gold statuette of an elf worth 100 gp. A non-evil creature grasping it can ask a question and receive a telepathic answer as though it had cast augury. Each creature can activate it only once, ever.
book: Phandelver and Below: The Shattered Obelisk

name: Chime of Exile
description: This silver chime is engraved with delicate sigils. While holding it, you can use an action to cast banishment (save DC 20); a target with 50 hit points or fewer automatically fails its save. Once used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Crown of Lies
description:
Burnished, entwined metal rods form this crown, which the Dark Powers of the Domain of Dread gave to Kas so he would deliver Vecna to them. To attune, place it on your head and speak a true desire of your heart.
Random Properties. 1 minor beneficial, 1 major beneficial, and 1 minor detrimental property.
Perfect Disguise. As an action, transform to look and feel exactly like any creature you've seen at least once that is no more than one size smaller or larger than you, voice included. Your size and speed become the creature's; you otherwise keep your statistics, and the crown melds into you undetectably. The form lasts until you die, your attunement ends, or you use another action to change form. Interactions reveal no illusion, and you count as that creature for spells, traps, and defenses. Your lies always seem true to any magical or mundane detection, you receive sending spells meant for you or the disguised creature, and scrying aimed at that creature targets you. Only a wish spell reveals your true nature. In your true form, you can make the crown visible or not.
Destroying the Crown. If its wearer is killed by the creature it is disguised as, the crown disintegrates.

name: Rod of Seven Parts
description:
The Wind Dukes of Aaqa wove their power into the Rod of Law to imprison the demon lord Miska the Wolf-Spider on Pandemonium; the rod shattered into seven pieces scattered across the multiverse.
Possessing the Broken Rod. It can't be attuned while broken. Holding a piece, you know the general location of the next consecutive piece. Pieces can be assembled or disassembled as an action, but a partial rod gains no other abilities. Each piece can cast its associated spell from the Rod Pieces table as an action, once per dawn.
Possessing the Whole Rod. Once all seven are reassembled, it can be attuned. It is a +3 quarterstaff. It has 7 charges and regains 1d4 + 3 daily at dawn: as an action, expend 1 charge to cast any spell from the Rod Pieces table, or cast detect evil and good at no cost. A non-lawful wielder finds their worldview shifting toward keeping a personal code.
Destroying the Rod. The assembled rod must be immersed in lava in the Abyss for fifty years. A single piece destroyed this way re-forms after one year and teleports to a random place in the multiverse.

name: Hammock of Worlds
description: A colorful hammock woven with traditional Ataguan designs, usable only by a member of the Green Doctors. As an action, unfold it on a solid surface to open a two-way portal to the Ghost Orchid Tepui in the Feywild or to the Drought Elder in the Far Realm (your choice). Folding it up as an action closes the portal. Once it has opened a portal, it can't do so again for 1d8 hours.

name: Azuredge
description:
An intelligent battleaxe forged by the archwizard Ahghairon to defend Waterdeep: a rune-etched steel handle wrapped in blue dragon hide with a star sapphire pommel, its silver, electrum, and steel head shimmering deep blue.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with it, and the shield spell offers no defense against it. A fiend or undead you hit takes an extra 2d6 radiant damage.
Hurling. It has 3 charges, regained daily at dawn. Expend 1 to throw it (range 60/180); hit or miss, it returns to your hand or feet at the end of the turn.
Illumination. As an action, make it glow blue (bright light 30 feet, dim light 30 more) or quench the glow.
Sentience. Lawful neutral, Int 12, Wis 15, Cha 15, with hearing and darkvision 120 feet. It speaks, reads, and understands Common, communicates telepathically with its wielder in a calm, delicate voice, and senses non-lawful creatures within 120 feet.
Personality. Sworn to protect Waterdeep, it patiently seeks a law-abiding wielder devoted to the city. If used against its will, it can become ten times heavier and adhere to any Medium or larger object or surface; only a wish spell can separate them without destroying one, though the axe can end this at any time.

name: Badge of the Watch
attunement_note: by someone designated by the Open Lord of Waterdeep
description: This badge marks a captain of Waterdeep's City Watch and bears the city's emblem. While wearing it, you gain a +2 bonus to AC if you aren't using a shield. If it is more than 5 feet from you for over 1 minute, it vanishes and reappears within 5 feet of the Open Lord. While holding it, the Open Lord knows your location on the same plane while you remain attuned, and can end your attunement by touching it as an action.

name: Blackstaff
attunement_note: by a Blackstaff heir, who must be a wizard
description:
The sentient, rune-carved symbol of office of the Blackstaff, Waterdeep's highest-ranking wizard. It has all the properties of a staff of power, plus the following.
Animate Walking Statues. Within the city, expend charges as an action to animate or deactivate one walking statue of Waterdeep per charge. Animated statues obey the telepathic commands of Khelben Arunsun's spirit within the staff, and go inanimate if deactivated or if the staff is broken.
Dispel Magic. Expend 1 charge as a bonus action to cast dispel magic on a creature, object, or effect you touch with the staff; against an unwilling creature or its possession, you must first hit it with a melee attack using the staff.
Drain Magic. When you hit a creature that uses spell slots with the staff, expend 1 charge as a bonus action to make it expend its highest-level slot.
Master of Enchantment. When you cast an enchantment spell of 1st level or higher while holding it, an Arcana check (DC 10 + spell level) lets you cast it without expending a slot.
Sentience. Neutral, Int 22, Wis 15, Cha 18, hearing and darkvision 120 feet, telepathy with its holder.
Personality. It holds the spirits of every previous Blackstaff, dominated by its devious creator Khelben. It protects Waterdeep and its Open Lord first and empowers its wielder second, and stops functioning for a Blackstaff who no longer serves its wishes until it finds a worthy heir.
Spirit Trap. A Blackstaff who dies is trapped in the staff and can't be raised. Destroying the staff frees the spirits, but Khelben can lodge in any remaining piece, which keeps Sentience and can remake the staff at will, trapping the spirits again.

name: Bracer of Flying Daggers
description: This armband appears to have thin daggers strapped to it. As an action, pull up to two magic daggers from it and hurl them immediately, making a ranged attack with each. A dagger not hurled at once vanishes, and they vanish after they hit or miss. It never runs out.

name: Dragonstaff of Ahghairon
description: While holding it, you have advantage on saving throws against the spells and breath weapons of dragons and the breath weapons of other dragon-type creatures. A dragon you touch with it can move through Waterdeep ignoring Ahghairon's dragonward until touched again or until a time you proclaim. It has 10 charges and regains 1d10 daily at dawn: expend 1 as an action to cast command, and a dragon targeted has disadvantage on the save.

name: Feather of Diatryma Summoning
description: Speak the command word as an action and throw this bright plume into a Large unoccupied space on the ground within 5 feet, and it becomes a living diatryma (an axe beak whose beak deals piercing damage) for up to 6 hours. It reverts early at 0 hit points or when you touch it and speak the word again as an action, and then can't be used for 7 days. It is friendly, can be ridden, understands your languages, and obeys your spoken commands, defending itself if given none.

name: Knave's Eye Patch
description: While wearing this eye patch, you have advantage on sight-based Perception checks, are unaffected by Sunlight Sensitivity, and are immune to magic that reads your thoughts or determines whether you are lying. Creatures can communicate telepathically with you only if you allow it.

name: Lord's Ensemble
attunement_note: by a creature with a humanoid build
description:
Worn by the Masked Lords of Waterdeep to make each indistinguishable from the others. The helm, amulet, and robe function as a single item, attuned together, but only within Waterdeep and its sewers.
Lord's Helm. A face-concealing bucket helm with eye screens. Your voice sounds genderless, and you are immune to magic that reads your thoughts, determines whether you are lying, or reveals your alignment or creature type. Telepathy reaches you only if you allow it.
Lord's Amulet. Bears the crest of Waterdeep and functions as an amulet of proof against detection and location.
Lord's Robe. Functions as a ring of free action and makes you appear a nondescript, androgynous humanoid 6 feet tall.

name: Paper Bird
description: Write a message of fifty words or fewer on this parchment and speak a creature's name, and it folds into a Tiny paper bird that flies to that recipient (turning to ash if they are on another plane). The bird is an object with 1 hit point, AC 13, flying speed 60 feet, Dex 16, 1 in all other abilities, and immunity to poison and psychic damage. It flies directly to within 5 feet of the recipient and becomes ordinary parchment that only they can unfold. It turns to ash if its hit points or speed drop to 0 or it is immobilized. Usually sold in boxes of 1d6 + 3 sheets.

name: Ring of Truth Telling
description: While wearing this ring, you have advantage on Insight checks to determine whether someone is lying to you.

name: Stone of Golorr
description:
A glossy greenish-gray palm-sized stone that is actually the aboleth Golorr, transformed into an object.
Random Properties. 1 minor beneficial and 1 minor detrimental property.
Legend Lore. It has 3 charges and regains 1d3 daily at dawn; expend 1 to cast legend lore, speaking directly with the aboleth, which can't lie but is often cryptic. It knows where Lord Neverember's secret vault lies, that three keys open it, and that the gold dragon Aurinax guards it.
Failed Memory. When your attunement ends, make a DC 16 Wisdom save or lose all memory of the stone and what it taught you. Remove curse has a 20 percent chance to restore it; greater restoration always does.
Sentience. Lawful evil, Int 18, Wis 15, Cha 18, hearing and darkvision 120 feet, telepathy with its attuned owner, and it learns the greatest desires of any creature communicating with it. It hungers for information, demands to be passed on often, and tries to take control of an owner who refuses.
Personality. Alien, domineering, and hungry for knowledge, it thinks itself an ageless god.
Destroying the Stone. It is immune to all damage and isn't a creature. Antipathy/sympathy cast on it, choosing antipathy against aberrations, turns it to mucus and releases Golorr within 30 feet, enraged and attacking all creatures it sees.

name: Demon Skin
description: This armor appears as a pot of bubbling black ichor. When you attune to it, the ichor contours to your skin and the pot vanishes; it can be worn under clothes and doesn't impede bodily functions. It can't be removed unless you choose to or die, at which point the ichor flows back into the reappearing pot. While wearing it, you have resistance to poison damage, and it doesn't impose disadvantage on Stealth checks.
book: Descent into the Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth

name: Iggwilv's Horn
description: As an action, blow this horn to cast arms of Hadar, fog cloud, gust of wind, or web from it (save DC 13). Each spell can't be cast from it again until the next dawn.
book: Descent into the Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth

name: Potion of Polychromy
description: Seven syrupy bands of brightly colored liquid. When you drink it, you and your gear take on a rainbow-hued appearance for 1 hour, during which you can use a bonus action to turn any colors you choose. Mimicking your surroundings makes your hues shift to match them, granting advantage on Stealth checks until you change colors or the potion ends.
book: Descent into the Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth

name: Tasha's Creeping Keelboat
description: A magic boat 10 feet wide and 30 feet long with four legs, giving it a walking and swimming speed of 20 feet (it can't go underwater). It moves at your spoken direction while you ride it, and creatures of your choice aboard gain a +1 bonus to AC. It carries 1,000 pounds without hindrance, or up to twice that at half speed.
book: Descent into the Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth

name: Book of Vile Darkness (Variant)
description:
A foul manuscript, most believe authored by Vecna, cataloging every vile idea and black magic he could find, with later additions stitched in by other evil writers. Plants wither near it, animals shun it, and even stone it rests on long enough crumbles.
An attuned creature must spend 80 hours studying it to gain its benefits and can then add evil lore to it. A non-evil creature that attunes makes a DC 17 Charisma save or becomes neutral evil. The book vanishes if you go 10 days without an evil act or willingly do good. If you die while attuned, a great evil claims your soul and you can't be restored to life while it is held.
Circle of Death. As an action, cast circle of death (DC 20); afterward roll a d6, and on 1-5 this can't be used again until dawn.
Condition Immunities. You can't be charmed or frightened.
Evil Presence. On attunement, its hostile spirit tries to possess you: on a failed DC 20 Charisma save you become an NPC under the DM's control until it is banished by dispel evil and good or similar magic.
Adjusted Ability Scores. After study, raise one score by 2 (max 24) and lower another by 2 (min 3), once.
Mark of Darkness. After study you gain a hideous disfigurement and advantage on Persuasion checks with evil creatures and Intimidation checks with non-evil ones.
Command Evil. While holding it, cast dominate monster (DC 18) on an evil target as an action, once per dawn.
Dark Lore. Double your proficiency bonus on Intelligence checks to recall lore about evil.
Dark Speech. As an action, recite Dark Speech: you take 1d12 psychic damage and each non-evil creature within 15 feet takes 3d6 psychic damage.
